* :recycle: Preserve categorical dtypes to reduce memory usage by ~5GB

Fixes excessive memory usage in historical_poverty step by preserving
categorical dtypes for string columns (country, region, region_old).

**Problem:**
- `np.asarray()` was converting categorical columns to object dtype
- Object dtype for 14M rows used ~3GB more memory per call
- Function called twice = ~6GB extra memory usage

**Solution:**
- Remove `np.asarray()` calls - use `.array` to preserve categorical
- Add dtype validation at function entry
- Add assertions to catch future regressions

**Impact:**
- String columns: 96-99% memory reduction (object → categorical)
- Total savings: ~5-6GB peak memory during execution
- Profiling mode verified: categorical dtypes preserved throughout pipeline

subject: ✨ Add CatalogPath helper class for parsing catalog paths (#5359)
message:
✨ Add CatalogPath helper class for parsing catalog paths (#5359)

* ✨ Add CatalogPath helper class for parsing catalog paths

Adds a pathlib.Path-like class for parsing and manipulating OWID catalog paths,
replacing ad-hoc string splitting throughout the codebase.

Features:
- Parse paths like `grapher/who/2024/gho/table#indicator`
- Properties: channel, namespace, version, dataset, table, indicator
- Computed properties: dataset_path, table_path, step_uri
- Builder methods: with_version(), with_indicator(), etc.
- Immutable (frozen dataclass) - can be used as dict keys

* 🐛🤖 fix: PREFER_DOWNLOAD for private datasets uses private R2 bucket

Since PR #5603 moved private dataset data files to a separate
`owid-catalog-private` R2 bucket, `_download_dataset_from_catalog`
was still hardcoding `s3://owid-catalog/` for all datasets. This
caused PREFER_DOWNLOAD to download only empty datasets for private
steps (only metadata was in the public bucket).

Fix: use `config.R2_BUCKET_PRIVATE` when `self.is_public` is False.

subject: 📊 Reduce CI log clutter (#5852)
message:
📊 Reduce CI log clutter (#5852)

* 📊 Reduce CI log clutter

* ✨🤖 Reduce CI log clutter (~15MB → ~3MB)

- Remove long_to_wide.skip log (20K lines of 'I did nothing')
- Aggregate DisplayNameWarning per table instead of per column (15K→~250 lines)
- Aggregate NoOriginsWarning per table instead of per column (4.7K→~100 lines)
- Change UN SDG per-variable logging from info to debug (6.8K lines)

* ✨🤖 Truncate column list in "Region already has data" warning

Was dumping full set of 500+ column names (e.g. WDI) into a single log line.
Now shows count + first 5 column names.

* ⚡🤖 Lazy-import jsonschema in grapher helpers

jsonschema pulls in rfc3987_syntax.syntax_helpers which takes ~560ms to
import. It's only used by _validate_grapher_config() which rarely fires.
Moving to a local import saves ~1.4s per step subprocess startup.

* ⚡🤖 Use fork() instead of subprocess for step execution

Every DataStep previously spawned a new Python process via
`uv run etl d run-python-step`, paying ~3-5s of startup overhead
per step (uv + Python + full import chain). For simple steps like
data://grapher that do ~30ms of actual work, this was 99% overhead.

Now on Linux (and macOS), we use os.fork() instead. The forked child
inherits all loaded modules instantly (~1ms), runs the step, and exits
— so leaked memory from feather serialisation still dies with the child.

Falls back to the old subprocess path when fork is unavailable or when
IPDB is enabled (debugger needs a proper subprocess).

Before: data://grapher step = ~3.5s (local), ~5s (CI)
After:  data://grapher step = ~0.1s

Estimated CI savings: ~19 min of step CPU time across 804 steps.

🐛🤖 Fix indicator upgrader stripping inheritance overrides that match schema defaults (#5911)

When a chart has inheritance enabled and the user explicitly sets a property
(e.g. hasMapTab=false) that happens to match the schema default but overrides
the indicator's ETL config (hasMapTab=true), the validate_chart_config_and_remove_defaults
step was stripping it. This caused the admin API to re-inherit the indicator's
value, re-enabling the map tab.

Fix: skip stripping schema defaults for inheritance-enabled charts. The admin API
correctly computes the patch by diffing the full config against the indicator's
ETL config, so it needs all explicit values preserved.

subject: 📜 Add chart-text-report skill (#5961)
message:
📜 Add chart-text-report skill (#5961)

* 📜 Add chart-text-report skill

* 📜🤖 Add chart-text-report skill

Skill that generates a compact Markdown audit of user-facing chart text
(Title, Subtitle, Footnote, description_short, description_key) for an
MDim, a grapher dataset, or a hand-picked list of indicators. Each field
is tagged [override]/[inherited]/[missing] so a reviewer can tell what
Grapher renders vs. what's defined in the ETL.

Codifies the non-obvious inheritance rule: chart-level FAUST must resolve
from presentation.grapher_config only — not from title, title_public,
display.name, or description_short.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ✨🤖 Disambiguate duplicate view headings + clean slug generation

When multiple MDim view groups resolve to the same chart Title, append
the differentiating non-collapsed dimension(s) as a `(Dim: Choice)`
suffix so every `## Title` heading in the report is unique.

Also treat underscores as word boundaries in description_key slug
generation so Markdown italic runs like `_pre-tax_` produce slugs like
`income-pre-tax-measured` instead of `income-_pre-tax_-measured`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* 📜🤖 Drop DB-free MDim rebuild helper; use etlr only

The user works on a staging server where MySQL is always up, so the
staging/production rebuild path (`etlr <mdim> --export --grapher` →
`Collection.save()` → `validate_indicators_in_db` + `upsert_to_db` +
`save_config_local`) is the only path that keeps local config in sync
with what the server actually publishes. A DB-bypass helper that
monkey-patches those validation calls produces configs that can
silently drift from DB state, so remove it along with all references.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* 📜🤖 Drop --grapher from the default MDim rebuild recipe

The FAUST report reads metadata directly from the local grapher-channel
feather files, so the slow grapher://<dataset> MySQL upload that
--grapher triggers isn't needed. Recommend `etlr <mdim> --export
--private` as the default — change detection still re-runs any garden
or MDim step that changed, so editing metadata yaml/py still takes
effect. Only reach for --grapher when indicator data/metadata needs to
land in MySQL for live rendering.

Observed: forced single-MDim rebuild drops from ~60s (with --grapher)
to ~4s; cached no-op rebuild is ~2s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* 🐛🤖 Fix three Codex-flagged issues in chart-text-report helpers

- Narrow exception handling in get_indicator_meta: only a missing
  column returns None (legit [missing] tag); malformed paths, wrong
  channel, missing datasets, unreadable feathers now propagate so
  broken state can't silently masquerade as [missing].
- Enforce grapher channel in get_indicator_meta: a garden/... path
  would previously be resolved against grapher storage (or reported
  missing) without warning; now we raise explicitly.
- Preserve explicit empty-string overrides in resolve_field: a view's
  `note: ""` (used to suppress an inherited footnote) was being
  dropped and falling back to the inherited value, so the report
  disagreed with what Grapher renders. Empty strings are now counted
  as real overrides, and render_value displays them as `_(empty)_` so
  the distinction from a plain missing field is visible.

Spot-check: 11 incomes_wid views + 2 gini_pip views now correctly
render their empty-footnote override instead of the inherited note.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ✨🤖 Conditionally emit source-tag legend entries

Only document `[override]`, `[inherited]`, `[missing]` in the "How to
read this file" section when the tag actually appears in the rendered
body. For example, now that the empty-string-override fix turned every
former `[missing]` footnote in the four inequality MDims into
`[inherited] _(empty)_`, the `[missing]` bullet no longer shows up in
those files' legends.

Mechanism: build the body first, scan with `collect_used_tags()`, then
emit `how_to_read_block(used_tags)`. Works for both the MDim script
and the dataset/indicator-list script.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: ✨ Add check-metadata-style skill (#5951)
message:
✨ Add check-metadata-style skill (#5951)

* ✨ Add check-metadata-style skill

* ✨🤖 Add check-metadata-style skill

New Claude Code skill that audits a grapher step's user-facing chart
metadata (titles, subtitles, descriptions, display names, attribution)
against OWID's Writing and Style Guide in Notion.

- Scoped to the current step (no whole-catalog audit).
- Fetches the guide via the Notion MCP at invocation time; no cached
  copy on disk.
- Prefers the rendered (post-Jinja) metadata from the built catalog so
  template artifacts are caught; falls back to ruamel_load on .meta.yml
  with a warning when the dataset isn't built.
- Skips description_from_producer (verbatim source text) and technical
  fields (unit, processing_level, …).
- Offers fix-all / review-each / cancel like check-metadata-typos; edits
  use ruamel_load/ruamel_dump to preserve comments.

* ✨🤖 Wire metadata checks into the update-dataset workflow

After all ETL steps are built (snapshot → meadow → garden → grapher),
the update-dataset skill now runs three metadata checks before moving
on to the indicator upgrade:

- /check-metadata-typos  (codespell on new .meta.yml files)
- /check-metadata-spacing (post-Jinja spacing artifacts in the catalog)
- /check-metadata-style  (Notion Writing and Style Guide audit)

Added as step 6b (mirroring the 1b check-outdated-practices slot) so the
existing 7–10 numbering stays intact, and added a matching entry to the
progress checklist.

* 🔨🤖 Replace Notion fetch with a committed STYLE_GUIDE.md

Per PR review: the style guide is edited rarely, so paying the Notion
MCP OAuth + fetch cost on every invocation is overkill. Switch to a
committed snapshot next to the skill — faster, offline, greppable, and
changes to the rules become a reviewable PR.

- Add STYLE_GUIDE.md (snapshot of the Notion page) alongside SKILL.md.
- Drop the Notion MCP auth/fetch flow from SKILL.md; instead read the
  local file.
- Note in SKILL.md and STYLE_GUIDE.md to refresh the file via PR when
  the Notion page changes.

* 📜🤖 Drop Notion MCP mention from update-dataset step 6b

The check-metadata-style skill now reads rules from a committed
STYLE_GUIDE.md next to its SKILL.md, so no Notion access is required
during an update. Point users to refresh that file from Notion in a
separate PR when it looks stale.

- Normalize step path inputs (strip data:// and etl/steps/data/) so the rendered-metadata loader doesn't silently fall through to the YAML-only fallback when users follow the Scope example.
- Split the step 6b rerun into garden/meadow and grapher variants, adding --grapher on the latter so metadata fixes propagate to staging before the indicator upgrade.

subject: :sparkles: Include snapshots in `etlr --watch` file watcher (#5946)
message:
:sparkles: Include snapshots in `etlr --watch` file watcher (#5946)

* 📊 Include snapshots in etlr --watch file watcher

* 🐛🤖 Include snapshots in etlr --watch file watcher

Previously --watch only observed changes under etl/steps/, so edits to
snapshot scripts or .dvc files were silently ignored. Generalize
watch_folder to accept multiple paths and also watch SNAPSHOTS_DIR.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ✨🤖 Auto-run etls on snapshot edits during --watch

When a .py or .dvc file under snapshots/ changes, run `etls` in-process
before rebuilding downstream steps so the watch loop fully refreshes the
data source.

Also refresh watch_folder's last_seen mapping after yielding, so that
file writes performed by the handler (such as etls updating a .dvc
checksum) don't falsely re-trigger on the next tick.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ✨🤖 Only auto-run etls when snapshot is in the watched subdag

Before running `etls` on snapshot edits during --watch, check that the
snapshot is actually a dependency of the steps currently being watched.
Unrelated snapshot edits are now skipped with an informative message
instead of triggering a potentially expensive (and irrelevant) download.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ✨🤖 Skip etls in --watch for manual-upload snapshots

Manual-upload snapshots (no origin.url_download or source.source_data_url
in the .dvc) require --path-to-file, which watch mode cannot supply. For
those, skip the etls step and fall through to the downstream rebuild so
metadata-only edits still propagate via the .dvc checksum.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ✨🤖 Handle driver-script snapshots in etlr --watch

A single snapshot .py can produce multiple .dvc files with unrelated
names (e.g. child_labor_report.py → child_labor_by_region.csv.dvc, …).
Treat a .py as related to the watched subdag if any .dvc in its
directory is in the subdag, not only when the stems match directly.

Also, fall through to the downstream rebuild when etls raises — so
metadata-only edits and driver-script edge cases still propagate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ✨🤖 Skip etls in --watch when .dvc edit is metadata-only

Before invoking etls on a .dvc change, compare the on-disk data file's
md5 with the md5 recorded in outs[0]. When they match, the edit touched
metadata only (title, description, etc.) and there is no reason to make
etls redownload potentially huge content — the .dvc checksum change
still propagates to the downstream rebuild.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ✨🤖 Watch only .dvc files under snapshots/ in etlr --watch

Simpler than auto-running etls: downstream steps key off .dvc checksums
already, so watching just the .dvc (not snapshot .py scripts) is enough
to pick up changes. The user runs \`etls\` manually in another terminal
when they want to refresh a snapshot, and the .dvc rewrite triggers the
watching etlr process to rebuild.

This drops the auto-etls integration entirely (and its edge cases:
driver scripts, manual-upload --path-to-file, metadata-only redownloads,
subdag filtering, graceful failure), leaving only the watcher extension
to the snapshots/ tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: :bug: Fix DoD hover in YAML files (#5950)
message:
:bug: Fix DoD hover in YAML files (#5950)

* 📊 Fix DoD hover in YAML files

* 🐛🤖 Ship dod-syntax v0.0.19 to fix broken DoD hover in YAML/Python files

The installed v0.0.18 only rendered the hover when a DoD was already
cached by preload, so first-time hovers never triggered a fetch. The
on-demand fetch fix was already in src/, but the version was never
bumped so `make vsce-sync` skipped the upgrade — bump to 0.0.19 so
everyone actually receives it.

* 🐛🤖 Fix DoD hover DB access by falling back to OWID_ENV

The fetch_dod.py script only tried ENV_FILE_PROD before falling back to
a hardcoded config (user=owid, no password, host=prod-db) that does not
match how ETL users connect to live_grapher (via the bore tunnel on
127.0.0.1:3310 with DB_USER=live_grapher, defined in .env).

Use OWID_ENV — already loaded from .env by etl.config — as the fallback.
This makes the hover work out of the box for anyone whose .env points at
live_grapher, which is the common case.

* 🐛🤖 Pin DoD fallback to live_grapher, not arbitrary OWID_ENV

Per Codex review on #5950: returning OWID_ENV from get_prod_env() when
ENV_FILE_PROD is unset silently follows whatever the developer has in
.env — local grapher, STAGING-overridden owid, etc. — so the extension
could query the wrong DB and show stale or missing DoDs.

Require an explicit production source in order: ENV_FILE_PROD, then
.env.prod by convention, then .env read raw via dotenv_values and only
accepted if DB_NAME=live_grapher (bypassing any STAGING override that
etl.config may have applied to OWID_ENV). Refuse to fall back otherwise.

Also fix the repo-root computation: the old etl_root = parent.parent.parent
actually pointed at vscode_extensions/, not the repo root, which would
have broken the .env and .env.prod lookups anyway.

* ✨🤖 Read DoDs from staging first; surface source in hover (v0.0.20)

DoDs are edited on staging first and synced to production later, so
the right DB for the hover while developing is the user's own staging
server — not live_grapher. The extension now walks a prioritized list
of candidate envs and uses the first one that accepts a connection:

  1. OWID_ENV when STAGING is set — developer's staging server.
  2. ENV_FILE_PROD.
  3. .env.prod in the repo root.
  4. .env read raw, only if DB_NAME=live_grapher.
  5. OWID_ENV as final fallback (local dev DB, etc.).

Each result carries a `source` label; the hover renders it as
`*Source: staging (staging-site-foo)*` whenever it's not production,
so users can tell where the content came from. Production reads stay
unannotated.

Falls through on `OperationalError` — "tunnel down" or "can't reach
staging" just tries the next candidate instead of erroring out.

Also bumps the extension to 0.0.20 and ships a fresh .vsix.

* ✨🤖 Always show DoD source in hover (v0.0.21)

Previously the hover only showed "Source: …" when the source wasn't
production, which meant a prod hover and a silent hover were visually
identical — there was no way to tell at a glance whether a hover was
reading from staging or from live_grapher. Show the source line
unconditionally so users always know which DB served the definition.

The PR went 0.0.18 → 0.0.19 → 0.0.20 → 0.0.21 while iterating on the
hover and the DoD source selection. Collapse those intermediate builds
into a single version bump — final shipped vsix is 0.0.19, containing
all of the latest code (staging-first DoD lookup with fall-through,
unconditional source label in the hover).

subject: 📊🤖 Update SIPRI military expenditure dataset (#5972)
message:
📊🤖 Update SIPRI military expenditure dataset (#5972)

* 📊 📊🤖 Update SIPRI military expenditure dataset

* 📊🤖 Update SIPRI military expenditure dataset

* Finish init

* 🔨🤖 Snapshot outs + skill emoji guidance

- Record md5/size/path for the new SIPRI military_expenditure
  snapshot (identical bytes to 2025-04-28 — SIPRI 2026 URL not
  live yet; real data lands on 2026-04-27).
- Update-dataset skill: swap the `📊🤖 for data updates` example
  for one that points at the emoji auto-prepended by `etl pr` +
  🤖. This avoids doubled category emojis in PR titles.

* 📜🤖 Update-dataset skill: catalog and re-evaluate NOTE/TODO markers

Carried-over # NOTE: / # TODO: comments in step files are almost always
"fix this when upstream fixes it" markers. Add a two-phase flow so
workarounds get revisited on every data refresh:

- Step 1c catalogs the annotations into workbench/<short>/notes_to_check.md
  (list only, don't act yet — fresh data isn't in yet).
- Step 6a re-evaluates each entry after grapher has run on the new data:
  delete the workaround + comment together if upstream is fixed, else
  note the status in the PR body.

* 📜🤖 Update-dataset skill: detect and review sanity_checks functions

Some garden steps (world_bank_pip, world_inequality_database,
luxembourg_income_study, etc.) run data-quality assertions inside a
`sanity_checks` function, often gated by a module-level boolean flag
(`DEBUG`, `SHOW_SANITY_CHECK_LOGS`) that defaults to False. On a data
refresh these checks are the most reliable way to catch silent quality
regressions, but only if someone remembers to enable the flag and read
the log.

Add:

- Step 1d: rg for sanity_checks functions + their log-control flags,
  record them alongside the # NOTE: / # TODO: catalog.
- Step 5b: after the garden run, flip the flag to True, re-run with
  stdout captured to workbench/<short>/sanity_checks.log, scan for
  assertion failures / anomalies, surface findings in the PR body,
  and revert the flag before committing.

Checklist and artifacts list updated.

* 📜🤖 Update-dataset skill: catch inline '# Sanity check' comments too

Sanity checks also live as inline comment-marked assertion blocks
(e.g. emdat/natural_disasters.py, emissions/national_contributions.py)
without a dedicated function. Broaden the step 1d sweep regex to catch
'# Sanity check(s)' comments, and split step 5b into two handling
paths: function-with-flag (flip flag, capture log, revert) vs.
flagless-function-or-inline-comment (step already passed assertions;
read the block to understand the invariant and spot-check qualitatively
on fresh data).

* 📜🤖 Update-dataset skill: handle logging-only sanity checks correctly

When trialing step 5b on wid/2026-02-10/world_inequality_database, the
DEBUG=True flag produced 11 warning/critical rows — 291 monotonicity
violations, 1551 out-of-bounds wealth averages, etc. — yet the step
still exited 0 because the checks log via paths.log.warning / .critical /
.fatal instead of raising.

The previous skill text said "step 5 passed means all assertions held",
which is wrong for this pattern. Clarify: a sanity check can enforce
either by raising or by logging; logging variants do not fail the step.
Tell the reviewer to scan stdout for warning keywords when the block
uses logging, and treat growing log warnings the same way as new
AssertionErrors.

* 📜🤖 Update-dataset skill: call out silent-delete sanity checks

Trialing step 5b on wb/2026-03-24/world_bank_pip revealed that its
sanity_checks function doesn't just log — it DROPS rows that fail
invariants (e.g. Cote d'Ivoire 2002 with non-monotonic shares in 2017
PPPs). With SHOW_SANITY_CHECK_LOGS=False the deletions still happen
silently; the flag only controls whether the reviewer sees which rows
went away.

Add a warning to step 5b: when reading a sanity_checks function, scan
for drop/filter/tb=tb[...] and list every deletion in the PR body, not
just the warning counts. If a deletion looks newly obsolete after an
upstream fix, that's a candidate for removing the workaround.

* Update military expenditure metadata: extend coverage to 2025 and adjust currency references to constant 2024 USD

Co-authored-by: Copilot <copilot@github.com>

* 📊🤖 Apply SIPRI 2025 release data and remove Sierra Leone workaround

Phase 2 of the military_expenditure update — real data from the SIPRI
2025 release is now in.

Snapshot:
- Downloaded the new SIPRI-Milex-data-1949-2025.xlsx; outs md5/size
  refreshed (e026e92113fd9981910edd4608a8ce7d, 922,808 bytes; +6%).

Meadow:
- Sheet name `Constant (2023) US$` → `Constant (2024) US$`.
- COLUMNS_TO_DROP for constant_usd_regions: `2024 (current prices)` →
  `2025 (current prices)`, `Unnamed: 39` → `Unnamed: 40` (new 2025
  column shifted the trailing blank by one).
- na_values: added Unicode ellipsis `…` (U+2026) to cover SIPRI's new
  missing-data sentinel; kept ASCII `...` for backwards safety.

Garden:
- Removed `correct_sierra_leone` workaround and both `# NOTE: Delete
  correction of Sierra Leone data when fixed` comments. SIPRI fixed
  the leone redenomination upstream — raw `share_govt_spending` for
  SL is now ~0.04 (was ~0.00003), so the ×1000 multiplier is no
  longer needed and would now produce 4000% values. Verified post-
  build SL values are in the 2.5–5.5% range, matching the corrected
  old-version numbers exactly.
- countries.json: added `Central and Western Europe` →
  `Central and Western Europe (SIPRI)`. SIPRI's `Regional totals`
  sheet now uses this merged label (replacing separate `Central
  Europe` + `Western Europe`); the per-indicator sheets still carry
  both old labels for historical continuity, so those mappings stay.

* 📜🤖 Update-dataset skill: add Wizard Anomalist + Chart Diff hand-off

After everything is committed (including the DAG archive), point the
user at the two staging-side QA tools:

- Anomalist: http://staging-site-<branch>/etl/wizard/anomalist
- Chart Diff: http://staging-site-<branch>/etl/wizard/chart-diff

These are human-judgment tools (visual review of variable anomalies and
before/after chart thumbnails), so don't auto-run them — just hand off
the links so the user can click through. The pages need a fresh staging
build so this is genuinely the last step.

Slot order matches the user's preference: Codex review → DAG archive →
Wizard QA hand-off.

* 🔨🤖 Archive old military_expenditure entries and reorder DAG

- Moved sipri/2025-04-28/military_expenditure (snapshot → meadow →
  garden → grapher) from dag/redistribution.yml to the bottom of
  dag/archive/redistribution.yml, preserving the section comment.
- Replaced the in-slot 2025-04-28 entries with the new 2026-04-27
  entries so the dataset stays grouped with its neighbours under the
  MILITARY section header.
- Removed the duplicate MILITARY block that etl update had appended at
  the bottom of the active file.

* 📜🤖 Update-dataset skill: fix staging hostname truncation

The staging hostname is NOT just `staging-site-<branch>` — branch
names get truncated to the first 28 chars (Cloudflare DNS limit) by
get_container_name in etl/config.py. So a 30-char branch like
`data-military-expenditure-2026` actually maps to the container
`data-military-expenditure-20`, hostname
`staging-site-data-military-expenditure-20`. Without this rule the
Wizard QA links handed off at the end of the skill point at a
non-existent host.

Document the four-step normalization (replace separators, strip
prefix, truncate to 28, strip trailing dash) and recommend using
`get_container_name(branch)` directly via a one-liner so the agent
gets the canonical name instead of building it by hand.

* 🐛🤖 Add share-indicator sanity check + fix Belarus 1992-2013 data

Added sanity_checks(tb) — logs a warning for any country/year where
share_gdp or share_govt_spending falls outside [0, 100]%.

Running the check on the new SIPRI 2026 release surfaced a real data
quality issue: Belarus share_gdp for 1992–2013 is inflated 1000× in
the new file (raw 9.3–18.3 vs. expected 0.0093–0.0183), producing
values of 928–1832% of GDP after the standard ×100 percentage scaling.
Cross-checked against:

- 2025-04-28 published values: 1.6–2.8% of GDP (matches the corrected scale)
- World Bank / CIA Factbook estimates: ~1–2% of GDP through this period

Added a correct_belarus(tb) helper that divides Belarus 1992–2013
share_gdp by 1000, restoring the correct scale, plus a
`# NOTE: Delete correction of Belarus data when fixed` marker so a
future updater knows to revisit this once SIPRI fixes the upstream
file. After the fix, only Kuwait 1991 (117% of GDP) remains as a
sanity-check warning — that one is a documented legitimate outlier
(post-Iraqi-liberation reconstruction spending against collapsed GDP).

* 🐛🤖 Make share sanity check raise + whitelist Kuwait 1991

Switch sanity_checks from log.warning to ValueError so future
regressions cannot land silently — the step now fails the build if
any share_gdp / share_govt_spending value falls outside [0, 100].

Add a KNOWN_SHARE_OUTLIERS whitelist so a single well-documented
legitimate value (Kuwait 1991, ~117% of GDP — post-Iraqi-liberation
defense spending against collapsed wartime GDP) doesn't block the
build. New entries flag genuine regressions — adding to the whitelist
requires a deliberate edit and a comment justifying the exception.

* 💄🤖 Move KNOWN_SHARE_OUTLIERS to module-level constants block above run()

* :sparkles: new snapshot

* 🐛🤖 Adapt sipri 2026 step to fixed snapshot

SIPRI's updated file adds ". ." as a new missing-data sentinel and
fixes the Belarus 1992-2013 share_gdp scaling upstream, so the local
correct_belarus workaround was active-harm and is removed.

message:
🐛 Self-heal partial dataset output to recover from interrupted runs (#6003)

* 🐛 Self-heal partial dataset output to recover from interrupted runs

* 🐛🤖 Self-heal partial dataset output to recover from interrupted runs

A directory left behind by an interrupted shutil.rmtree (no index.json,
leftover tables) used to crash every subsequent build at
_dataset_index_mtime → Dataset(...) → FileNotFoundError, requiring a
manual rm -rf on the host to unblock deploys.

DataStep.run now detects this state at the top of the method and clears
it before any read; the existing post-failure cleanup is unified onto
the same helper. Dataset.create_empty renames the dir aside before
rmtree so a partially failed deletion can never leave the original path
in a half-deleted state again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* 🐛🤖 Use uuid suffix for cleanup temp dir

Address codex review: a deterministic `.tmp.<pid>` suffix could collide
within the same process if rmtree(ignore_errors=True) left a leftover
temp dir behind, breaking subsequent retries until manual cleanup.
Switch to uuid4 so each attempt gets a fresh path.

🐛 fix `make docs.build` zensical type error (#6048)

* 🐛 fix `make docs.build` zensical type error

* 🐛 fix `make docs.build` — set comprehension, not list

The inline monkey-patch of `zensical.config._list_sources` in `docs.build` and
`docs.serve` returns a list (`[(f,h) for ...]`) but zensical's downstream
`_apply_defaults` then unions it with two sets via `|`, which fails:

    TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for |: 'list' and 'set'

The original `_list_sources` returns `set[tuple[str, int]]`. Switch the
comprehension to `{(f,h) for ...}` to preserve the set type.

* 🐛 fix `make docs.build` & clean up doc warnings

  type (`type(r)(...)`) instead of always returning a set, so the result
  remains a `Sequence` for the downstream Rust struct extraction. Fixes the
  list-vs-set mismatch in CI.
- pyproject.toml: drop `[tool.uv] exclude-newer = "3 days"`. uv requires an
  RFC 3339 datetime here, not a duration; the line caused a parse-error
  warning on every uv invocation and caused the [tool.uv] block to be
  silently ignored anyway.

📊 Update carbon pricing data (#6058)

* 📊🤖 Update RFF carbon-pricing data to 2026-05-08

Updates the World Carbon Pricing (WCP) and Emissions-weighted Carbon Price
(ECP) datasets to the latest upstream release. Both datasets share snapshots
and are released together by Resources for the Future, so they are bumped
together.

Adapts to a major upstream restructure: both repos renamed master→main, WCP
now serves data under versioned subdirs (v2026.1), and ECP moved its outputs
to `_output/_dataset/` with date-suffixed filenames. The IPCC sector-codes
auxiliary file was removed from upstream entirely; replaced the previous
cross-zip workaround with a dedicated `ipcc_codes.csv` snapshot pinned to a
commit on ECP's `ej-path-edits` side branch where the file still exists.

Year coverage extends from 2024 → 2025 across both datasets, and the ECP
coverage table now starts at 1970 (was 1989). New sub-national entities
(79–83 Mexican states, Japanese prefectures, and Chinese SARs) added to the
excluded-countries file. Garden's economy/coverage equality assertion
softened to a warning since they now diverge slightly upstream.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* 🐛🤖 Fix: use ECP variable-weights file (ecp_vw), not fixed-weights (ecp_fw)

In v2026.1 the upstream ECP repo split the per-country economy file into
three methodological variants: ecp_intro (narrow), ecp_fw (fixed weights,
pinned to a base-year emission share), and ecp_vw (variable / time-varying
weights). The first cut of this update incorrectly picked ecp_fw, which
produced zeros for countries with newly-introduced carbon taxes covering
sectors that had small base-year emission shares — most visibly Argentina,
South Africa, and Uruguay (whose price collapsed from $123 → $0), and to a
lesser extent Canada and China.

Empirically, ecp_vw is the methodological successor to v2025.0's single
ecp_CO2.csv: values match within ~$1 across France, Germany, UK, Sweden,
Japan, Canada, China, and Mexico. Switching to ecp_vw restores the affected
countries and brings the global emissions-weighted price back into line
with v2025.0 (now $6.68 in 2025, was $4.92 with ecp_fw).

Slack announcement and /latest post drafts updated with corrected headline
numbers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

The upstream ECP README states explicitly that "all prices in this
repository are expressed in 2021USD/tCO2", with 2019 being only the FX
conversion year (LCU→USD), not the inflation base. Both the old (v2025.0)
and new (v2026.1) READMEs say the same thing — the old ETL metadata had
this wrong all along. Corrected the unit string on all six price-related
indicators.

* 📊 Migrate UN SDG snapshot/meadow/garden/grapher to origins

* 🔨🤖 Migrate UN SDG chain from sources to origins

Snapshot DVCs (un_sdg.feather, un_sdg_dimension.json, un_sdg_unit.csv)
rewritten from flat top-level legacy fields (`source_name`,
`source_published_by`, `publication_year`, `url`, `source_data_url`,
`license_url`, etc.) to modern `meta.origin:` blocks.

Grapher step refactored:
- Loads the snapshot's origin via Snapshot(...).metadata.origin (the
  per-snapshot origin can't be carried on DatasetMeta — that class has
  no `origins` field — so reading the snapshot directly is the
  pragmatic propagation point).
- Per dynamically-generated variable: builds an Origin with the cleaned
  underlying-source name (FAO, WHO, ILO, …) as producer, and the rest
  of the fields (title, citation_full, url_main, dates, license) from
  the snapshot's origin. Sets `origins=[origin]` on each VariableMeta
  instead of the legacy `sources=[source]`.

Grapher meta.yml: dropped the `un_origin` YAML anchor + the
`sources: []` / `origins: [*un_origin]` overrides on the two named
indicators (they replicated what now flows naturally from the snapshot).
Meadow meta.yml: dropped the duplicate `dataset.description`
(inherited from origin).

* 🐛🤖 Attach origin to sdgs_urbanization garden columns

The `un_sdg` chain migration (f717242a50) updated the 2023-08-16 grapher to
synthesize per-column origins from the snapshot, but missed the parallel
sdgs_urbanization chain that branches off the same meadow. Its grapher step
then failed `grapher_checks` because neither column carried origins.

Load the snapshot origin directly in the garden step (same pattern as the
un_sdg grapher) and attach it to each indicator column after the pivot.

* 🔨🤖 Propagate un_sdg snapshot origin through meadow → garden → grapher

Read the snapshot via `snap.read_feather()` in the meadow step so the
snapshot's origin is attached to every column. From there origins flow
naturally:

- meadow now operates on Tables (uses `pr.to_numeric` for the numeric
  filter on Value) instead of casting to pd.DataFrame.
- The un_sdg garden step still relies on the legacy DataFrame pipeline,
  so it captures `base_origin` from the meadow's `value` column before the
  cast and re-attaches it to each output table's `value` column.
- The un_sdg grapher reads `base_origin` off the garden table's `value`
  column instead of reloading the snapshot directly.
- The sdgs_urbanization garden step no longer needs its own Snapshot()
  load — the origin survives meadow → meadow → garden via column metadata.

message:
🐝 Switch PyPI publish workflow to Trusted Publishing (OIDC) (#6107)

* 🐝 Switch PyPI publish workflow to Trusted Publishing (OIDC)

* 🔨🤖 Switch PyPI publish workflow to Trusted Publishing (OIDC)

Replace the long-lived POETRY_PYPI_TOKEN_PYPI secret with PyPI Trusted
Publishing. The publish job mints a short-lived OIDC token instead of
holding a permanent API token, removing the single highest-value secret
in this repo's blast radius for supply-chain attacks.

- Add top-level `permissions: contents: read` baseline.
- `publish` job: `environment: pypi` + `permissions: id-token: write`
  so OIDC can mint a token for the trusted publisher configured on PyPI
  for each of owid-catalog / owid-datautils / owid-repack.
- Replace `uvx twine upload` with pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish (pinned to
  commit SHA). PEP 740 attestations are emitted automatically.
- Build via `astral-sh/setup-uv` + `uv build` (replaces the unpinned
  `curl … | sh` uv installer).
- Bump and pin to commit SHAs: actions/checkout v6.0.2,
  actions/setup-python v6.2.0, astral-sh/setup-uv v8.1.0,
  pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish v1.14.0.
- Build a dynamic matrix in `detect-changes` so unchanged packages don't
  spin up publish jobs (and don't trigger the environment approval).
- Add `fail-fast: false` so one package failing doesn't cancel others.

Tracked in owid/ops#472. Post-merge cleanup: delete the
POETRY_PYPI_TOKEN_PYPI secret from repo settings and revoke the
matching API token on PyPI.

subject: 🐛 Hash canonical JSON for metadataChecksum to stop false-positive chart-diff (#6135)
message:
🐛 Hash canonical JSON for metadataChecksum to stop false-positive chart-diff (#6135)

* 🐛 Hash canonical JSON for metadataChecksum to stop false-positive chart-diff

* 🐛🤖 Stop spurious chart-diff METADATA CHANGE on VariableMeta shape flips

`calculate_checksum_metadata` previously hashed the live `VariableMeta`
dataclass via `hash_any`, which walks `dataclasses.fields(...)`. So when
a field was added, renamed, or removed — even with `None`/`[]` defaults
that get stripped by `_omit_nullable_values` before reaching S3 — the
checksum would flip while the on-disk JSON didn't change a byte. Result:
chart-diff lit up every chart as METADATA CHANGE with an empty UI diff
after #6081 (Remove Source metadata object) landed.

Hash the pruned dict (`variable_meta.to_dict()`) instead. `@pruned_json`
collapses None/empty values exactly like `_omit_nullable_values` does in
the JSON-upload path, so the checksum now matches what the comparator
actually sees. Added a regression test covering the empty-field-shape
invariance.

The whole grapher DB needs re-upserting once this lands so every row's
metadataChecksum is recomputed under the new scheme.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* 📜🤖 Note metadataChecksum to_dict() perf cost in comment

Per-call cost is ~130µs vs the prior ~57µs (~3×), dominated by
DataClassJsonMixin.to_dict(). Negligible against the surrounding S3 and
MySQL writes, so leaving as-is for now; comment points at the fast-path
trick (inline-pruning field walker, mirror of `dataclass_from_dict`)
should profiling ever flag it.

Malawi broadcasting), others are general prosecution-discretion clauses
or domestic-violence statutes. Replace the over-specific previous
wording with a more honest version:

* 🐛🤖 Stamp extracted rows with SNAPSHOT_YEAR, not datetime.now().year

Codex P2: \`extract_from_api\` and \`create_long_dataset\` were stamping
\`year_extraction\` (and the current-status year range) with the
calendar year at run time. Rerunning the fixed snapshot path
\`lgbt_rights/2026-05-14\` in a later calendar year would have
silently rewritten those columns and extended current-status rows
into future years — same snapshot path, different data.

Derive the year from \`SNAPSHOT_VERSION\` instead. With
\`SNAPSHOT_VERSION = "2026-05-14"\`, \`SNAPSHOT_YEAR = 2026\` always.
A re-run on the same snapshot path now produces the same data
regardless of when it's executed; bumping the snapshot version is
the only way to advance the year.

The currently-uploaded snapshots are unaffected (they were produced on
2026-05-15, when datetime.now().year was also 2026).

subject: 📊 Center the rolling-average smoothing in historical_poverty (#6179)
message:
📊 Center the rolling-average smoothing in historical_poverty (#6179)

* 📊 Center the rolling-average smoothing in historical_poverty

* ✨🤖 historical_poverty: center the rolling-average smoothing

Switch smooth_estimates from a trailing 10-year window to an 11-year
centered window and anchor both endpoints (EARLIEST_YEAR and
LATEST_YEAR_PIP_FILLED - 1) to the original values.

The trailing window biased every decadal point upward, because the
monotonically declining poverty series leant on the higher-poverty
preceding decade. On the interpolated Ginis (World), the mean absolute
deviation from the original drops from ~0.8 pp to ~0.15 pp at $10 (and
the systematic direction disappears).
